title: Ceviche
subtitle: Peruvian lime-cured raw fish
excerpt: Peru's national dish: very fresh white fish cut into small cubes and marinated in fresh lime juice until the surface turns opaque, mixed with red onion, coriander, and chilli. The acid does the work; there is no heat involved, and it must be eaten fresh.

recipe.sourceNotes: Ceviche is considered the national dish of Peru and is officially celebrated on a national holiday in June. Its origins are pre-Columbian: the Inca are thought to have marinated fish in fermented chicha or passion fruit juice. The modern form with lime juice dates from the arrival of citrus fruits after the Spanish conquest. Peruvian ceviche is distinguished by its short marinating time (the Peruvian style is a quick cure of 3 to 5 minutes in very fresh fish, producing something between raw and cooked in texture) and by the use of ají amarillo, a fruity Peruvian yellow chilli. The liquid produced by the curing process is called leche de tigre (tiger's milk) and is drunk or used in cocktails. The fish must be the freshest possible; ceviche is not a suitable use for fish that is not impeccably fresh.

content.text: The fish must be impeccably fresh, from a trusted source, on the day of purchase. Cut it into pieces no larger than 2 cm so the acid can reach the centre quickly. The Peruvian style marinates for just 3 to 5 minutes; longer and the texture becomes firmer and more cooked-tasting. Taste a piece at 3 minutes and decide.

items.preparation: very fresh; skin and pin bones removed; cut into 2 cm cubes; use sea bass or other firm white fish
red onion; very thinly sliced; rinsed in cold water to reduce bitterness

content.text: Put the fish in a bowl. Season generously with salt and add the grated garlic. Pour the lime juice over and stir gently to coat all the fish. Leave for 3 to 5 minutes, stirring once.
Taste a piece; the surface should be opaque and the texture should have changed but still be yielding and not rubbery. If you prefer a firmer cure, leave for up to 10 minutes total.

Add the sliced chilli, drained red onion, and coriander. Toss gently. Taste and adjust salt and lime. Serve immediately in chilled bowls with the curing liquid (leche de tigre). Do not leave to stand; the texture deteriorates within 15 minutes.
